transcript.content: Hello, welcome to the clinic. What brings you in to see me today?

I’m here because I’m losing a lot of time rechecking things. Like dressing supplies, door locks, file dimensions, revision notes… I keep going back over them, and I don’t feel like I can move on until I’ve done the same routine enough times that the anxiety finally drops.
Do you have unwanted thoughts or images that keep coming into your mind?

Yes. Even when I know I’ve cleaned the wound area properly, or I’ve already reviewed a CAD file, this thought cuts in like, what if I missed one tiny thing? And then my mind jumps to it becoming an infection, or a design mistake that could hurt someone. I can tell myself I checked it, but it doesn’t really go away just because I reason with it.
Do you avoid certain situations or activities because of these unwanted thoughts or anxiety?

Yeah… I think I do, or at least things are getting pushed out because of it. My project deadlines have started slipping because I stay late trying to feel okay enough to submit work. And outside of work, I’ve stopped making it to paddleboarding meetups or workouts because the checking routines take up the time I used to keep for myself.
Are you feeling overwhelmed by these thoughts and checking behaviors to the point where they are interfering with your relationships or daily life?

Yeah, it is interfering. Work is the clearest example—my project deadlines are starting to slip because I stay late trying to get comfortable enough to submit things. And outside of work, I’ve stopped making it to paddleboarding meetups or workouts because the routines just eat up the time I used to keep for myself.
Do you feel anxious or on edge even when you're not actively checking or thinking about the things that worry you?

I’m not totally sure. I think most of the anxiety is tied to the checking or the “what if” thoughts. If I’m distracted or doing something else, I don’t always feel on edge, but I haven’t really paid close attention to that.
Do you feel anxious when you're not thinking about the things that you check?
I’m not really sure. I haven’t noticed it as much when I’m not thinking about the checking stuff. It feels like the anxiety mostly shows up when those thoughts come in, but I’m not sure beyond that.
Do you feel anxious when you're not thinking about the things that you check?
I don’t really know. I haven’t paid enough attention to it to say for sure. It seems like the anxiety is mostly connected to the checking thoughts, but outside of that, I’m not sure.
Do you feel anxious when you're doing something you enjoy and not thinking about the things you check?

When I’m really into something I enjoy, I don’t think I notice feeling anxious as much. But I’m not completely sure—I haven’t really tracked it closely. It seems more like the anxiety comes up when the checking thoughts show up.
Do you feel anxious when you're not having any of these checking thoughts?
I’m not really sure. If I’m not having the checking thoughts, I don’t think I notice much anxiety, but I haven’t paid close enough attention to say for certain.
Is there ever a time when you feel anxious without any specific worries or checking thoughts present?

I’m not sure. I can’t really think of a clear time where I felt anxious with no specific worry there. Usually if I notice it, it’s tied to the checking thoughts, but I might not always catch what started it.
Can you think of any situation where you felt anxious without having any of these specific checking thoughts or worries?

I can’t really think of one clearly. Most of the time, if I’m anxious, there’s some thought behind it—like even after I know I cleaned a wound area, or checked over a CAD file, this thought cuts in that I missed one tiny thing. Then it feels like it could turn into an infection or a design mistake that hurts someone, and I can’t really reason it away.
Do you ever feel anxious without any specific thoughts or worries?

Not really that I can point to. When I feel anxious, it usually comes with a specific thought—like even if I know I cleaned a wound area or reviewed a CAD file, this thought pops in that I missed one small thing, and then it could become an infection or a design mistake that hurts someone. I can’t really just reason it away.
Do you feel anxious for no reason at all, without any thoughts or worries?

No, not really for no reason. It’s usually that same kind of thought cutting in—like I know I cleaned the wound area or checked the CAD file, but then I get stuck on the idea that I missed one tiny thing and it could turn into an infection or a mistake that hurts someone. I can’t really talk myself out of it.
Do you ever feel anxious without anything specifically worrying you?

No, I don’t think so. It’s usually tied to a specific worry. Like I’ll know I cleaned a wound area or looked over a CAD file, but then this thought keeps coming back that I missed one tiny thing, and that it could turn into an infection or a mistake that hurts someone. I can’t really reason my way out of it.

No, not really. It’s not like anxiety comes out of nowhere for me. There’s usually a thought attached to it—like I’ll have cleaned a wound area or checked a CAD file, and then I keep thinking maybe I missed one tiny thing, and that could lead to an infection or a design mistake that hurts someone. Even if I know I already checked, I can’t just reason it away.
Is your anxiety always triggered by one of these specific checking thoughts or worries?

Yes, pretty much. It’s usually that specific kind of thought—like even after I know I cleaned the wound area or reviewed a CAD file, my mind keeps saying I missed one tiny thing.
